description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problem categories and their corresponding educational levels from the MathOdyssey benchmark dataset. The chart consists of 12 distinct slices that do not appear to be ordered by size. There is no separate legend, nor are there percentage labels inside the slices; instead, each segment is identified by an external text label connected by a thin grey line, detailing the category, educational level, percentage, and raw count in parentheses. None of the slices are visually emphasized through exploding or offsetting. Starting from the top left and moving clockwise, the largest slice is dark blue and labeled "Algebra - [grey rectangle] - 21.19% (82)". This is followed by a light blue slice for "Statistics – University-level – 4.39% (17)", a cyan slice for "Probability – University-level – 5.43% (21)", an olive green slice for "Differential Equations – University-level – 3.62% (14)", a grey slice for "Calculus and Analysis – University-level – 6.20% (24)", and a pink slice for "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level – 6.46% (25)". Continuing clockwise, a brown slice represents "Pre-Calculus – High School – 14.21% (55)", a light purple slice denotes "Geometry – High School – 3.62% (14)", and a salmon-colored slice accounts for "Algebra – High School – 17.83% (69)". The remaining slices include a light green segment for "Combinatorics – Olympiad-level – 9.56% (37)", a light orange segment for "Geometry – Olympiad-level – 6.46% (25)", and finally, a very thin pale blue segment for "Number Theory – Olympiad-level – 1.03% (4)".
